name: datasette-tildepair-v2
instr:
Row keys in `?_shape=object` come back in the wrong format for tables with a two-column primary key

A small sync job of ours reads stock levels from Datasette. It pulls
`/inventory/stock.json?_shape=object` (primary key is warehouse + sku) and turns each key back into
the warehouse and sku the way the docs describe row identifiers: split on commas, tilde-decode
each part. Since we moved to this checkout, every key looks like `EU~2FWest~2CSKU-1~2E5` instead
of `EU~2FWest,SKU-1~2E5`, so the job sees one value per row and skips the lot. The tables we have
with a single-column key are fine.

The checkout is in /workdir. Could you track down where this actually goes wrong and fix it
there? Please include a regression test, somewhere under tests/ (say tests/test_repro.py), that fails on the current code because
of this problem (a real test failure, not an import error) and passes once it's fixed.
Test the reported behaviour, not your patch: it should still pass if the bug gets fixed some other correct
way, so no asserting on source text or on helpers only your fix has. It should run on its own
from a clean checkout with just your test files added.

I doubt I'm the only one hitting this. Anything else that goes through that code is probably
wrong too, so please fix it at the source rather than special-casing my input. The fix belongs in
the code itself, not in the tests. CI runs the full test suite on every change,
so it shouldn't break anything else.
